parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: providers, mcp, schedules, hooks, memory, or profiles

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Rolling days selected by turn start time

post.summary: Run a browser tool through the same permissions and transcript as a model call.

BackgroundTaskInfo.description:
Process-local child-agent work associated with one parent conversation.
Child threads and their transcript are durable; the live/background flag
intentionally is not and disappears when the server process stops.

CommandExecutionResponse.description:
Tagged result of the shared command dispatcher. Prompt commands create a
normal turn; workflow commands return the durable run; management commands
such as `/workflow list` and `delete` return concise text.

CommandInfo.description: A user-defined slash command served from markdown files.

plugin.description: Contributing plugin, when this command came from a plugin bundle.

source.description:
Registry source. `workflow` identifies a dynamically discovered
workflow invocation; absent values are configured prompt commands.

summary.description:
Caller-provided summary. When absent the server generates one with the
thread's model using the hidden `compaction` agent profile.

tailStartSequence.description:
Runtime-owned retained-tail boundary. API callers may omit this; the
server computes it from the configured recent-turn count.

oneOf.description:
Runtime-owned exact task state. API callers may omit this; the server
always replaces it with the current durable state before committing.

CreateThreadRequest.description:
Unset fields resolve to configured defaults on the server, falling back to
the built-in `build` agent and the current default OpenAI model.

DefinitionExecution.description: Execution semantics shared by discovered commands and skills.

oneOf.description:
Topmost ancestor of `thread_id`: equals `thread_id` for root threads,
and the root of the parent chain for child-agent threads. Lets clients
follow everything belonging to one root conversation.

ExecuteCommandRequest.description:
Execute one name from the authoritative server command registry. Unlike
`StartTurnRequest::command`, this contract can dispatch both configured
prompt templates and durable workflows without overloading the stable turn
endpoint.

arguments.description:
Plain command tails use a JSON string. Workflow callers may supply
typed JSON directly, preserving booleans/numbers/objects end to end.

variant.description:
Workflow child-agent variant (for example `high` or `xhigh`). Prompt
commands use `reasoning_effort` instead.

FileDiff.description:
Bounded file-change payload shared by Git review and snapshot/turn diffs.
Git responses normally carry `patch`; snapshot responses normally carry
`before` and `after`. A missing body with `truncated=true` remains an
honest metadata-only change instead of returning an unbounded payload.

encoding.description: utf8 (default) or base64 for binary uploads.

oneOf.description: Original source item, not its newly assigned ID in the fork.

sequence.description: Last copied sequence, or zero for a fork with no copied history.

title.description: Source title at creation, retained when the source is unavailable.

oneOf.description:
Semantic fork boundary. When set, copy history strictly before this
user-message item so clients can restore and edit that prompt.

title.description: Title for the fork; defaults to "Fork of {parent title}".

upToSequence.description:
Copy parent items up to and including this sequence; defaults to all.
May accompany `before_item_id` as a compatibility fallback when it is
exactly the sequence immediately before that user message.

goal.description: Compatibility mirror for clients that consumed the original `{ goal }` API.

logicalTurn.description:
Zero is the user-triggered iteration; positive values are autonomous
continuations already reflected by `GoalState::turns_used`.

GoalLogicalTurnPhase.description:
Observable boundary for one provider-facing goal iteration. Haarness may
execute several logical goal turns inside one durable user turn; this event
preserves the lifecycle distinction without manufacturing transcript
messages or nested durable turns.

awaitingUserInput.description:
Runtime circuit breakers set this only when the next ordinary user
message should naturally resume the pursuit. Manual and budget pauses
deliberately keep it false.

lastBlockerTurn.description: Logical goal-turn number on which the blocker recurrence was last counted.

InputQueueAction.description:
All edits compare the whole queue revision. A stale client must refresh,
never silently overwrite another client's edit or an already-delivered input.

attachments.description:
Local media paths, file URLs, or data URLs attached to this
message. `images` remains accepted when reading older databases
and API clients.

queued.description:
True when the message arrived while a turn was already running and
was queued for steering into that turn's next provider round.

synthetic.description:
Internal prompt injected by the runtime rather than authored by the
user. Clients hide it from transcript/history surfaces while the
provider still receives its text as normal context.

oneOf.description:
Durable boundary recording that a queued user message was included in
a provider-round snapshot. The original message keeps `queued=true` as
provenance; this marker is its transient-queue acknowledgement.

Durable navigation edge between a parent `task` call and the child
thread it created. Live `task.updated` events carry progress, while
this item keeps completed children reopenable after the turn or a
client restart.

Durable lifecycle checkpoint for a task that may outlive the parent
tool call. This keeps background state reconstructable after an SSE
gap or client restart without treating the launch acknowledgement as
the child's final result.

state.description: running | background | done | failed | cancelled | interrupted

always_patterns.description:
Generalized rules an "always" answer would persist,
e.g. `bash:git status *`.

patterns.description: Exact things being asked about (command texts, paths, globs).

custom.description: Permit free-form text alongside the listed choices.

multiple.description: Select any number of choices before submitting one reply.

tail_start_sequence.description:
First raw transcript item retained verbatim after the summary.
Sequence numbers remain stable inside a thread and across forks.

oneOf.description:
Exact task-list state at this compaction boundary. Older records
decode without a checkpoint; a present checkpoint with an empty
list intentionally clears all prior todos.
A workspace file snapshot captured before a turn's first mutation.

base_snapshot_id.description:
Present on a completion checkpoint and points to the matching
pre-mutation checkpoint. Undo applies only this bounded delta.

boundary_sequence.description:
Transcript sequence immediately before the mutation group guarded
by this snapshot. Older records omit it and use legacy inference.

LazyToolMode.description: Controls whether non-essential tool schemas are loaded on demand.

oneOf.description:
Sets a durable live override. Omit or send null to return to the
configured/default mode, matching per-tool availability reset semantics.

LoopConfig.description:
A recurring prompt attached to a thread: re-submitted `interval_seconds`
after each completed turn until `expires_at`.

choices.description: Empty for free text, otherwise an enumerated choice.

data.description: Structured resource state for clients that render their own controls.

cwd.description: Working directory for a local MCP process or a dynamic header helper.

env.description: Environment passed only to a local stdio MCP child process.

headers.description: Headers attached to every remote Streamable HTTP request.

headersHelper.description: Claude Code-compatible command that prints a JSON header object.

oauth.description:
Generic public MCP OAuth. `None` auto-detects OAuth for Streamable HTTP;
`Some(false)` disables discovery for servers using another auth scheme.

oauthClientId.description: Optional public client id for servers without dynamic registration.

oauthScopes.description: Explicit OAuth scopes. Empty lets MCP discovery select server scopes.

timeoutMs.description:
Optional connection/helper timeout. Plugin `timeout` seconds are
normalized to milliseconds by configuration discovery.

reasoningEfforts.description:
Concrete reasoning-effort names accepted by this model/provider pair,
ordered from lightest to strongest. An empty list means callers must
leave the effort unset and use the provider default.

PendingPermissionInfo.description:
One unanswered permission prompt, listable so clients can repopulate
pending approvals after a reconnect or thread switch — including prompts
raised on child-agent threads.

alwaysPatterns.description: Rules an "always" answer would persist, e.g. `bash:git status *`.

patterns.description: Exact things being asked about (command texts, paths, globs).

PendingQuestionInfo.description:
One unanswered model question, listable so clients can hydrate every
prompt in a root conversation after reconnecting or switching threads.
Questions raised by parallel child agents remain distinct queue entries.

action.description: install | update | enable | disable | remove | marketplace

source.description:
`haarness` for installed bundles; `haarness-global` or
`haarness-local` for directly loaded Haarness plugin directories.

ProjectInfo.description: A durable project groups one primary checkout and any linked Git worktrees.

root.description:
Primary checkout for a Git project, or the registered directory for a
non-Git project.

PromptUsage.description:
Text estimates from the final prepared request, after request hooks.
Provider framing and binary media tokens are not included.

PtyCursor.description: Text control frame sent before replay and whenever the output cursor moves.

QueueInputRequest.description:
User input against a thread that may already have a running turn. When a
turn is active the text is persisted immediately and steered into that
turn's next provider round; otherwise a normal turn starts.

delivery.description: Steer by default for compatibility; queue waits for an idle boundary.

synthetic.description:
Internal runtime prompt, hidden from user-authored transcript/history
surfaces but still delivered to the provider.

queued.description: True when the message was queued into an already-running turn.

baseSnapshotId.description:
Workspace state produced by undo. Redo uses it as the expected side of
a conflict-checked delta before restoring `snapshot_id`.

sequence.description: Items after this sequence soft-delete when the next turn starts.

snapshotId.description: Pre-revert backup snapshot consumed by unrevert.

defaultProvider.description:
Effective workspace configuration, for choosing a concrete model before
creating a conversation. These are preferences, not credentials.

eventCursor.description:
Latest published event id. Snapshot-first clients capture this before
hydration, then replay only deltas after the snapshot boundary.

defaultAgent.description: Effective primary agent for new conversations; absent on older servers.

attachments.description:
Local media paths, file URLs, or data URLs. Kept as string sources so
local-first clients do not have to persist large base64 blobs.

autoApprove.description:
Non-interactive caller explicitly authorizes permission prompts for
this turn. Scheduled runs set this after the schedule itself has been
approved; ordinary REST/TUI clients leave it false.

command.description:
Name of a custom slash command; the server expands its template with
`text` as the argument string and may switch agent/model per its
frontmatter.

synthetic.description:
Internal runtime prompt. Backward-compatible API clients omit this and
receive ordinary user-message behavior.

tools.description:
Per-turn tool visibility and execution policy. Missing names retain
their normal availability; `false` both removes a tool from the
provider schema and hard-denies a fabricated call.

oneOf.description: Durable boundary between copied history and a fork's own continuation.

isSubagent.description: Delegated agent conversation; forks retain parent lineage but are not subagents.

oneOf.description:
Present while the thread sits in a reverted state (undo pending
confirmation by the next turn).
Schedule that created this run; independent of its editable title.

ultracode.description: Standing workflow-orchestration preference for subsequent turns.

TodoCheckpoint.description: Versioned exact todo state carried across a lossy prose compaction.

revision.description:
Sequence of the latest todo snapshot, or zero when the exact state is
known to be empty without a prior todo write.

priority.description:
Priority. Older persisted todo items did
not carry it, so decoding them defaults to medium.

ToolCatalogEntry.description: One provider-visible or deferred tool in the current runtime catalog.

advertised.description: Whether this schema would be sent on the next matching provider round.

enabled.description: False means the tool is unavailable at both schema and execution time.

essential.description: Essential tools stay resident when lazy loading is active.

estimatedTokens.description: Deterministic provider-schema estimate; deliberately labeled as an estimate.

group.description: Stable functional grouping such as `core`, `agents`, or `extensions`.

loaded.description: Whether this session explicitly promoted a deferred tool.

source.description: `native` or the projected MCP server id.

ToolSettingsUpdate.description: Live, durable workspace-scoped tool policy update.

enabled.description: `Some` sets an override; omitted removes the persisted override.

ultracode.description:
This turn runs with workflow-orchestration guidance. The flag is
durable and provider-independent; runtimes resolve it to the strongest
supported reasoning effort (or the provider default).

sourceHash.description: SHA-256 of the immutable source snapshot.

agent.description: Immutable workflow-wide child-agent defaults captured at launch.

oneOf.description:
Conversation that launched this run. Execution itself happens in the
run's dedicated `thread_id`; this scope keeps progress notifications
attached to the conversation that requested the workflow.

source.description: Immutable source snapshot used by restart-from-beginning resume.

WorkflowStartRequest.description:
Start one durable workflow run. Exactly one of `name`, `source`, or `path`
must be supplied. Named runs use the statically discovered catalog; inline
and explicit-path runs are intended for the model-facing workflow tool and
still pass through the coordinator's trust and permission boundary.

agent.description:
Workflow-wide child-agent defaults. Individual `ctx.agent` calls and
phase model/variant metadata retain higher precedence.

oneOf.description:
Launching conversation. The coordinator creates a dedicated workflow
child session so tool and agent activity stays inspectable.

wait.description:
Wait for a terminal state before returning. REST/TUI starts normally
leave this false; the CLI can request synchronous execution.

WorkspaceCleanupRequest.description:
Explicitly remove a stale managed-workspace registration after its checkout
has disappeared. This is intentionally a distinct endpoint so an older
server cannot interpret cleanup as ordinary worktree deletion.

WorkspaceInfo.description:
A concrete directory with its own server, session database, and runtime
lease. `managed` means Haarness created it and may reset/remove it.

exists.description:
Refreshed when the registry is read; missing directories remain visible
so users can explicitly clean up stale metadata.

WorkspaceRefInfo.description:
One named Git ref that can be selected as a new workspace's base.
`reference` is the unambiguous, fully-qualified value clients should send
back; `name` is the concise label intended for display.

current.description: True only for the local branch used by an omitted/blank `fromRef`.

WorkspaceRefKind.description: The Git namespace a discoverable workspace base belongs to.

WorkspaceRefsResponse.description: Discoverable named bases for the current workspace's owning project.

defaultRef.description:
Stable value recorded by create when `fromRef` is omitted or blank:
the primary checkout's current branch, or its exact detached commit.

confirm.description: Required acknowledgement that the checkout directory will be removed.

deleteBranch.description:
Delete the worktree branch after removal. Git's safe `-d` check still
refuses an unmerged branch.

discardChanges.description: Permit removal when tracked or untracked changes exist.

confirm.description:
Required acknowledgement that commits on the worktree branch may be
moved back to its base ref.

removeUntracked.description: Permit deleting untracked (but never ignored) files.

toRef.description: Override the workspace's recorded base ref for this reset.

WorkspaceResolveRefRequest.description:
Resolve an arbitrary Git ref to the commit a workspace would start from.
Missing and blank values deliberately use create's default-base behavior.

DiffTruncation.description:
Why a reviewed file arrives without its body. `truncated` says *that* a
body is missing; this says *why*, so a client can tell "too big to review
here" from "there is nothing textual to show".

omittedFiles.description:
Changed paths the response does not list at all, because the review
hit its file bound. The response is an array with no envelope to hang
this on, so every returned entry repeats the same count and a client
renders it from whichever row it happens to hold. Absent when the
review listed everything that changed.

ReviewFile.description:
One entry of a Git review: a [`FileDiff`] plus the bounds the review had
to apply to produce it.

It flattens, so the wire shape is a strict superset of `FileDiff` and the
endpoint keeps returning the same array of the same objects; both added
fields are optional and defaulted, so an older client — or the generated
TypeScript SDK before it is regenerated — decodes these responses
unchanged and simply does not see them.
